personal.name: Tharan Suresh
personal.title: Graduate Research Assistant
personal.bio: I am a Ph.D. candidate in Movement & Cognitive Rehabilitation Science at The University of Texas at Austin, investigating the neurophysiological mechanisms underlying human motor learning and control. My research focuses on understanding how brain rhythms, particularly sensorimotor mu oscillations, influence our ability to learn new movements and retain them.

news.description: Successfully proposed my dissertation on sensorimotor mu phase-dependent mechanisms of motor learning.
Presented research on motor sequence learning at the Brainbox Initiative Webinar.
Gave a talk on 'The Human Machine: Discovering the wonders of how we move' at Morton Elementary School, Marysville, MI.
Presented on mechanisms of human motor learning and memory at the 2nd ReproRehab Research Summit, USC.
Advanced to Ph.D. candidacy at The University of Texas at Austin.
Delivered talk on 'The magic of movement and memories' at Science National Honor Society, Houston.
Presented research on practice-dependent corticospinal plasticity at Non-invasive Brain Stimulation conference, Gandhinagar.
